hints: Notice each diagram shows three quarks, so add the three quark charges to get the hadron charge.
Recall the quark charges: $u$ is $+2/3e$, while $d$ and $s$ are each $-1/3e$.
Test which combination of $u$, $d$ and $s$ shown in A to D sums to exactly $+1e$.
walkthrough: Each hadron contains three quarks, so its total charge is the sum of the three quark charges.
For hadron D the composition is $u+s+u$, so $Q = +2e/3 - e/3 + 2e/3$.
This simplifies to $Q = +3e/3 = +e$, which is the required charge of the $\Sigma^+$ particle.
The other hadrons give $-e$ for A and B, and $0$ for C, so they cannot be $\Sigma^+$. This is option D

options.C: Quarks $u+s+s$ give $(+2/3-1/3-1/3)e = 0$, so the hadron is neutral.
